description: Inbound delivery window of a purchase order (Ricardo's po-delivery-window map; Vince's Packaging Procure-to-GL Map stages 11 PO, 13 production complete and pickup, 16 receive): the PO issued, the supplier's confirmation (document-derived, optional), the vendor shipped (optional), and the goods received, which is due by the PO's planned arrival. It keeps planned arrival, actual shipment and actual receipt apart and never repairs a date. Chosen for an unnamed call when every root PO is open by the shared purchase-order status definition (open_when, operating.po_status: a Portal header not cancelled or draft whose lines' received quantity is below the ordered one, or a BC PO not fully received and not Draft; a Sage-only PO, an FM header alone, or an unmapped word is unknown, so it stays purchase_to_invoice unnamed); otherwise named calls only (implicit false). The receipt stage's lateness reads every requested-by date (FM datearrive and Sage exparrival first, then Portal expected_date, then the BC header requestedReceiptDate: the authority precedence of PurchaseOrder.expected_date; never a BC line's expected date or a supplier promise), the supplier's promised dates and the receipts. Not stages, because the ontology declares no record for them: map stages 01-10 (inquiry to requisition), 12 vendor prepayment, 14 packing slip / CI / BOL (a document lead only), 15 in transit, 17 landed cost, 18 relief; 19 G/L is purchase_to_invoice's.

open_when.note: The status values the shared definition reads: the Portal header holds the FileMaker words (Cancel, Complete, DRAFT, Pending, B.Order, Revised, Generated) and openness is by its lines' quantities (plx-customer-portal@d39d91b open-po-lines/route.ts:38-46,302-312); an FM header alone has no received quantity and a Sage iscomplete value is not mapped, so both stay unknown; BC reads fullyReceived and status (Draft: not issued).

stages.label: Purchase order
stages.description: The PO is issued by the shared purchase-order status definition (operating.po_status: a draft is not issued, a cancelled PO is not live, an unmapped word is unknown), or an FM, Sage or BC purchase order record.

evidence.note: The FileMaker generated_purchase_order and BC purchaseOrder headers read by the shared definition (operating.po_status), never by existence, as in purchase_to_invoice: an FM DRAFT or BC Draft is not issued, Cancel is ignored, an unmapped or null word leaves the stage unknown.

stages.label: Supplier confirmation
stages.description: The supplier confirmed the PO (order confirmation / proforma invoice). Portal and BC record none (runner.ts po.sent_unconfirmed_3d; map stage 13: vendor confirmation and PI number are Missing), so the evidence is a document-derived SupplierConfirmation read from captured mail attachments and SharePoint files (ontology/document_fields.py) and linked to the PO it names. Such a link is a lead: reported in the stage's gap, never counted as present; a reviewed link counts. Optional: receiving never waits on it.

evidence.note: Document-field links (SupplierConfirmation.confirms, ontology/document_fields.py store_document_links) and recorded reviews; a machine-read reference alone is a lead, never evidence.

stages.source_note: plx-customer-portal:portal/src/lib/work-routing/runner.ts@c3ffda3 (po.sent_unconfirmed_3d: "The portal records no vendor confirmation and no sent-at"); operating/process_stage_map.json stage 13.

stages.label: Vendor shipped
stages.description: The vendor shipped the goods (Portal 'Mark vendor shipped' records shipped_at; Vince's map stage 13, closest record: no cargo-ready status exists). Optional: Portal records it for origin INCO terms only, so receiving never waits on it.

stages.label: Receipt
stages.description: Goods were received against the PO (a receipt record of the PO; of its verified twin only when the PO's own system holds none): the actual arrival, never the expected one.

due.note: The PO's requested-by date (Vince: the lateness reference): FM datearrive, Sage exparrival, Portal expected_date and the BC header requestedReceiptDate (BC API v2.0 purchaseOrder), of the PO and its twins. A BC line's expectedReceiptDate follows the promised date when one is set, so it is the due date only when no header holds one (earliest open line); the lateness lines report it as the line's expected date. Different dates are reported, never chosen (Ricardo's header-vs-copy ETA disagreement); lateness names the governing one by precedence and cites it, or reports it missing.

lateness.note: Precedence mirrors PurchaseOrder.expected_date's authority (fm_bronze, sage_bronze > gold_etl_from_fm > bc). A promise is a SupplierConfirmation's delivery date (a machine-read lead; its link counts at the graph's tier floor only), ordered by the confirmation's document date: a later differing one is the revision.
